rounds.text: Manba Finance Ltd demonstrates robust top-line and bottom-line compounding, with 5-year sales growth at 26% and 3-year profit growth reaching an impressive 44% [E14, E18]. The company's profitability metrics comfortably outpace sector benchmarks, featuring an ROA of 2.47% versus the 1.9% sector median and an ROE of 11.07% compared to the 4.91% sector benchmark [E8, E9]. Valuation remains conservative relative to these fundamentals, trading at an attractive P/E of 13.9x and an EV/EBITDA of 8.52x, which sits well below the sector benchmark of 13.11x [E1, E11]. A discounted cash flow model suggests significant undervaluation with intrinsic value estimated at Rs 415 per share, offering a substantial 65.8% margin of safety against the current market price of Rs 142 [E32, E33]. Furthermore, the reverse DCF indicates that the market price currently prices in a modest 3.2% earnings growth, vastly underappreciating the company's historical trajectory [E34]. Technical strength supports this fundamental value, as the stock trades above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with a relative-strength rating of 87 [E37, E38]. Conceded: operating and free cash flows turned heavily negative in March 2026 at negative Rs 378 Cr and negative Rs 379 Cr respectively [E25, E26].

Despite headline earnings growth figures, Manba Finance Ltd carries severe fundamental risks highlighted by a catastrophic collapse in liquidity, evidenced by operating cash flow of Rs -378 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -379 Cr in Mar 2026, leading to an alarming cash conversion ratio of -8.40x [E24, E25, E26]. Institutional exodus further undermines the stability of the register, as foreign institutional holdings plunged from 5.16% in Sep 2024 to 1.07% in Sep 2026, while domestic institutions completely exited their 3.26% stake down to 0.00% over the same period [E29, E30]. The company's underlying financial quality is strained, explicitly flagged by filed statements for a low interest coverage ratio and a low return on equity of 13.3% over the last 3 years [E48, E49], alongside algorithmic warnings that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E55]. Furthermore, the stock trades at a price-to-book ratio of 1.7x, representing a premium over the sector benchmark of 1.29x [E7], and delivers a poor Sharpe ratio of 0.19 coupled with an annualised volatility of 34.7% [E41, E42]. Conceded: [E14, E15, E16, E17, E18, E19, E32, E33, E34]

Conceded: [E24, E25, E26, E29, E30, E48, E49]. Despite the cash flow figures and institutional exits noted, the company trades at an attractive P/E of 13.9x and EV/EBITDA of 8.52x, both well below their respective sector benchmarks of 18.76x and 13.11x [E1, E6, E11]. While the bear highlights a P/B premium against a sector benchmark [E7], the absolute price-to-book remains modest at 1.64x [E2], and the business comfortably outperforms sector medians with an ROA of 2.47%, ROE of 11.07%, and ROCE of 10.85% compared to sector benchmarks of 1.9%, 4.91%, and 5.42% [E8, E9, E10]. Furthermore, the discounted cash flow model indicates an intrinsic value of Rs 415 per share against a market price of Rs 142, offering a substantial margin of safety of 65.8% [E32, E33]. The reverse DCF demonstrates that today's price prices in a mere 3.2% earnings growth against an 18.0% base case [E34], while a rules-based screen scores the stock a solid 81 out of 100 with a BUY recommendation driven by strong YoY net profit growth of 27% [E50, E51]. Technical indicators also dispute the bear's gloomy narrative, showing the price trading above both its 50-day and 200-day moving averages with positive institutional money flow and a strong relative-strength rating of 87 [E31, E37, E38].

Conceded: [E1, E2, E6, E8, E9, E10, E11, E32, E33, E34, E37, E38, E50, E51]. The bull’s reliance on low multiples and strong valuation models ignores severe, fundamental structural strains explicitly flagged in the record. The company's operating cash flow for March 2026 collapsed to a staggering negative Rs -378 Cr, resulting in an abysmal cash conversion ratio of -8.40x and a free cash flow of negative Rs -379 Cr [E24, E25, E26]. Furthermore, filed statements explicitly warn that the company suffers from a low interest coverage ratio and a low return on equity of 13.3% over the last 3 years, while screening systems explicitly note that earnings growth is actively decelerating [E48, E49, E55]. Institutional confidence has simultaneously evaporated, evidenced by foreign institutional holding plunging from 5.16% in September 2024 to just 1.07% in September 2026, and domestic institutions completely abandoning the stock down to 0.00% [E29, E30]. Finally, despite technical momentum metrics cited by the bull, the historical profile shows a painful peak-to-trough drawdown of -46.6% alongside a weak Sharpe ratio of just 0.19, demonstrating that the underlying risk-adjusted reality diverges sharply from optimistic valuation models [E40, E42].
